items.question: Does C# if() treat 0 as false like JavaScript?
items.answer: No. The condition must be bool. You must write if (count > 0), not if (count). This is a compile error, not a run-time surprise — one of the biggest traps for developers coming from JavaScript.
followUps: How do raw string literals help with JSON test fixtures?
items.sixtySeconds: if needs bool. Literals are typed: 1.5 is double, 1.5m is decimal. Raw strings since C# 11 for JSON and CSV without escape noise.

items.question: What is new about ?. in C# 14?
items.answer: It can appear on the left of assignment or compound assignment. The right-hand side runs only if the receiver is not null. Increment and decrement (++/--) are still not allowed on ?.
followUps: Does JavaScript allow optional chaining on the left of =?
items.sixtySeconds: C# 14: x?.P = e assigns only when x is non-null; e is skipped otherwise. Different from ??= which assigns when the left value is null.

items.question: Why does a C# switch not fall through like C or JavaScript?
items.answer: Implicit fall-through is a compile error. You must use break, return, throw, or goto case. Stacked case labels (case 1: case 2:) share one body but are not statement fall-through.
followUps: When do you pick foreach over for?
Is goto ever acceptable in C#?
items.sixtySeconds: Must break/return/throw/goto case. foreach for sequences; for for indexes. goto case is the honest fall-through.

items.question: What does checked do? What about nameof(List<>)?
items.answer: checked throws OverflowException on integral overflow instead of wrapping. nameof is a compile-time rename-safe string. C# 14 allows unbound generics so nameof(List<>) is "List". sizeof is for unmanaged value types only.
followUps: Is the default arithmetic context checked or unchecked?
Can you use sizeof on a class?
items.sixtySeconds: Default wraps silently; checked throws. nameof is rename-safe; C# 14 unbound generics. sizeof not for reference types.

items.question: What is #nullable compared to #if?
items.answer: #if removes code from compilation based on defined symbols like DEBUG. #nullable toggles nullable reference type analysis warnings — it does not change run-time behavior. Full Nullable Reference Type (NRT) rules are in module 07. The #: directives on file-based apps are SDK config, not preprocessor directives.
followUps: Where should DEBUG-only RabbitMQ dry-run logging live?
Why is #region not a design tool?
items.sixtySeconds: #if strips tokens at compile time. #nullable is a warning switch. #: in file-based apps is SDK config, not #if.

items.question: When should you use foreach versus for?
items.answer: Use foreach when you need every item in a sequence and the index does not matter. Use for when the index is part of the business rule — skipping a CSV header, windowing, or parallel index math. Do not Add to a List during foreach — the enumerator throws.
followUps: What is the difference between while and do-while?
How does continue work inside a foreach?
items.sixtySeconds: foreach for sequences; for for indexes. do-while runs at least once. continue skips to the next iteration.

items.question: How does C# == compare to JavaScript == and ===?
items.answer: C# == is always strict and typed — like JavaScript ===. There is no loose == that coerces types. Comparing incompatible types is a compile error. Use decimal for money, not == on double without context.
followUps: Does TypeScript inherit JS == at run time?
When should you use ReferenceEquals instead of ==
items.sixtySeconds: C# == equals JS ===. No coercion. string == compares content. Reference types: == may be overridden; ReferenceEquals is identity.

items.question: When is goto acceptable in production C#?
items.answer: Rarely, but goto case is the honest way to share switch handlers. goto is forbidden across try/finally boundaries. Prefer structured control flow; cite goto case when discussing classic switch fall-through.
followUps: What jump statements exit a switch?
How does break differ inside foreach versus switch?
items.sixtySeconds: goto case for explicit switch sharing. break/return/throw exit switch. No goto out of finally. Early return beats deep nesting.
